rows.claim: force_flush calls all configured processors and aggregates errors. shutdown delegates to shutdown_with_timeout with five seconds; subsequent shutdown returns AlreadyShutdown. OTelSdkResult aliases Result<(), OTelSdkError>. Flush does not end live spans.
signatures: pub fn shutdown_with_timeout(&self, timeout: Duration) -> OTelSdkResult

/// A specialized `Result` type for Shutdown operations.
pub type OTelSdkResult = Result<(), OTelSdkError>;

rows.inference: Flush operates on processor queues, so callers must finish/drop spans and await producing tasks first; provider force_flush is not a span-completion operation.

rows.claim: SimpleSpanProcessor exports sampled spans on end with futures_executor::block_on; force_flush is a no-op success because it has no queue. This supports deterministic in-memory export probes after span completion.

The standard BatchSpanProcessor selected by with_batch_exporter uses a dedicated background thread. Exporter transports can impose their own runtime requirements. Shutdown is blocking; pinned docs advise a separate thread or spawn_blocking for current-thread Tokio runtimes.

InMemorySpanExporter is Clone and shares captured spans. get_finished_spans clones the collected SpanData values. Its default builder resets records on shutdown. keep_records_on_shutdown is crate-private and cfg(test), so consumers must read or clone records before provider shutdown.

rows.version_note: Upstream manifest strings are semver requirements, not equality pins. Portable probes may pin =0.31.0 and =0.32.0 explicitly.

rows.claim: tracing 0.1.44 Instrument::instrument wraps the future with a selected span; in_current_span captures Span::current at wrapper construction. The span is entered on each poll and on drop. Use these wrappers to propagate span context across async execution.

tracing 0.1.44 WithSubscriber is available with std. with_current_subscriber captures the default dispatcher when called; WithDispatch sets that dispatcher as the thread default for each future poll. It propagates subscriber context, while Instrument propagates span context.
signatures: fn with_subscriber<S>(self, subscriber: S) -> WithDispatch<Self> where S: Into<Dispatch>
rows.inference: For a per-session dispatcher used with spawned tasks, wrap the spawned future with both the intended span and current subscriber. A thread-local set_default guard alone does not install that subscriber on other worker threads.
